result.verdict: Not ready. The core draft-approval card is clear, and most error states name a recovery action, but round 2 is not reviewable as a complete 20-state set, two Send paths remain live while the draft is changing, several other states imply the wrong tap, and the legally-critical first consent shown is for Speech—not for the model provider the founder must approve before first use. A non-technical, one-handed founder cannot reliably tell what happened, what is blocked, and what happens next in the archived, running, group, computer-control, and Inner views.

findings.element: 'Send' button on 'Re: Pilot timeline' card in 'Agent editing the draft' frame
findings.problem: While the pill reads 'Updating' and 'Edit' is dimmed, 'Send' stays full-white and enabled. The founder can approve and send a stale version while the agent is literally rewriting it—the exact race the explicit-approval promise must prevent.
findings.norm: Approval actions must be disabled, with reason, whenever the object being approved is mutating; the safe action gets the visual prominence.
findings.fix: Disable Send and Edit during Updating, relabel the pill 'Updating draft—Send unavailable', and re-enable Send only with a visible 'Draft updated' change note.

findings.element: 'Send' on approval card vs up-arrow in composer 'Add Jordan on Cc' in 'Approval pending, typing' frame
findings.problem: Two different send actions coexist: 'Send' would mail the card still addressed only 'To Ana Ruiz', while the typed 'Add Jordan on Cc' has not been applied and its up-arrow sends a chat instruction. One tap on the prominent Send mails without Jordan on Cc.
findings.norm: One verb, one target, one prominent action per view; pending edits to an approval object must be applied or explicitly excluded before approval.
findings.fix: When composer text references the draft, disable the card Send and show 'Apply Cc change first', or merge the flows so the arrow updates the card and only then arms Send.

findings.element: Left sheet 'Share recordings with Speech A?' / 'Allow'
findings.problem: The brief's mandatory first step is consent to share data with the AI model provider, but the only first-use sheet in this file consents to Speech A for transcription. No model-provider sheet—named provider, data sent, retention—is shown at all, so the persona's first-visit journey cannot be verified or completed as specified.
findings.norm: Gate the first agent run on an informed, provider-specific consent naming recipient, data categories, and consequence of declining.
findings.fix: Add/show the Model consent sheet before first chat ('Share messages and attachments with [Provider]?'), and keep Speech consent as a separate, later, mic-triggered ask.

findings.element: Whole state grid: frames below 'Composer with an oversize file / New messages / Loading / Could not refresh'
findings.problem: The 'Archived', 'Read only', 'Session ended' and 'Reconnecting' states announced for round 2 appear only as cut-off footer labels with no frames, and ts_row2 was not supplied. Half the recovery story (notably session-ended and read-only) literally cannot be judged or learned from.
findings.norm: Every labeled state in a review board must be fully visible at legible size; error/terminal states need cause plus next step.
findings.fix: Re-export complete, uncropped rows for Archived, Read only, Session ended and Reconnecting, each showing its banner, composer state and single recovery action.

findings.element: 'Send' (up-arrow) button in oversize-file composer 'Attached the pilot deck.'
findings.problem: The composer states 'pilot-deck.pdf is over 25 MB. Remove it to send.' yet the round up-arrow remains solid white, signalling ready-to-send. Pressing it will presumably fail again; the affordance contradicts the instruction.
findings.norm: A blocked primary action must look blocked and name the blocker at the point of action.
findings.fix: Grey/disable the arrow until the red pilot-deck.pdf chip is removed, or make the tap animate/highlight the offending chip.

findings.element: 'Thursday works for me.' bubble in 'Offline, nothing queued' frame
findings.problem: Under a banner 'Offline. Messages send when you reconnect.' a normal right-aligned bubble sits with no status. The frame title says nothing is queued, but the founder cannot tell whether this bubble was already sent or is waiting—the queued frame differs only by tiny grey 'Waiting to send' text and omits the offline banner entirely.
findings.norm: Every unsent message carries a persistent per-message status; global connectivity and per-message state must agree in all frames.
findings.fix: Show the offline banner in both frames and label the bubble itself 'Sent earlier' vs 'Waiting to send' with a clock icon at readable contrast.

findings.element: 'Attached the pilot deck.' bubble with 'pilot-deck.pdf, 48 MB' in 'Refused: file too large'
findings.problem: Recovery copy 'Not sent: File is over the 25 MB limit / Remove file' is good, but the attachment keeps the shape of a successfully sent user bubble, so at a glance between meetings it reads as delivered.
findings.norm: Refused content must be visually quarantined (error styling, not success styling) until resolved.
findings.fix: Keep the red outline used in the 'Failed' bubble, add a 'Not sent' chip on the attachment itself, and only restore normal styling after a successful resend.

findings.element: 'Archived' frame: top bar 'Archived / Restore' plus composer 'Restore to send messages'
findings.problem: The saved messages inexplicably read as an already-completed exchange ending 'Sent. Anything else for Ana?' with no draft card, and the founder gets two competing recovery cues: a small top-right 'Restore' pill and a fake-looking text field that is not a field. Which to tap, and what restoring does to the pending draft, is unstated.
findings.norm: A read-only/archived state has one clearly labelled recovery action and explains what is preserved.
findings.fix: Replace the composer with a single full-width 'Restore chat' button and a line 'Your unsent draft to Ana is kept'; hide or mark the historical thread as read-only.

findings.element: 'Replaced by a newer draft' pill in 'Draft replaced' frame
findings.problem: The pill announces replacement but offers no 'View previous draft', undo, or diff. A founder who had reviewed the earlier wording loses it silently and must re-read the new card line-by-line to know what changed.
findings.norm: System-generated replacement of user-reviewed work must be recoverable and show what changed.
findings.fix: Make the pill tappable: 'Replaced by a newer draft — See changes', highlighting changed lines in the new card with Restore previous as secondary action.

findings.element: Stop (round square) as the only composer action in 'Running, text typed' frame
findings.problem: The founder has typed 'Also check Ana' but the sole button is the white stop square. There is no send affordance and no hint whether typed text queues, interrupts, or is discarded if they tap stop—one-handed, the big white target invites the destructive tap.
findings.norm: While an agent runs, composer behaviour (queue follow-up vs steer vs blocked) must be explicit and the destructive stop must not be the only prominent target.
findings.fix: Show an up-arrow 'Queue' action beside a smaller labelled Stop, with helper text 'Sends after this run' under 'Also check Ana'.

findings.element: 'Stopping' frame: spinner in composer, 'Message Inbox agent' placeholder, '•••' agent bubble
findings.problem: Nothing says 'Stopping…', how long it takes, or whether typing is accepted; the enabled-looking composer invites input into a dying run. The founder cannot tell if the tap registered.
findings.norm: Transitional states need a named label, disabled or clearly-queued input, and a terminal confirmation.
findings.fix: Add an inline 'Stopping the agent…' status above the composer, disable send, and end with 'Stopped—nothing was sent'.

findings.element: 'Team computer' card: empty black preview, 'Inbox agent is using it', 'Take control'
findings.problem: A blank black rectangle, an unexplained 'Team computer' concept and 'Take control' as the sole prominent action. A non-technical founder cannot see what the agent is doing with invoices, what taking control interrupts, or how to stop it safely—yet this is the spend-adjacent surface.
findings.norm: Remote/autonomous sessions require a live, legible preview, current action narration, and clearly separated Pause/Stop/Take-control.
findings.fix: Render the actual computer view with a caption 'Opening invoice list…', and offer 'Pause agent' as primary with 'Take control' secondary and explained.

findings.element: 'Not sent: No model connected' + 'Connect' under the 'Hello' bubble
findings.problem: The explanation of this state sits in a footnote outside the device frame ('Connect opens the Connect sheet; the message sends when it succeeds.'). Inside the product the founder only sees failure plus 'Connect'—no provider choice, cost, or consent implication, and 'No model' is developer language for this persona.
findings.norm: All explanatory copy must live in the UI; blocked-agent states explain in user language what connecting means before opening any sheet.
findings.fix: Use 'Not sent: no AI service connected yet' with an in-frame subline 'Connect to send—your message is saved and will send automatically'.

findings.element: Right panel toggles 'Model A / Speech A / Memory A' in 'Settings, AI data sharing'
findings.problem: 'Model A', 'Speech A', 'Memory A' are spec placeholders, not provider names a founder can consent to; nothing states retention, training use, or where 'Privacy details' leads. 'Turning off Model A pauses all agents.' appears only as a footnote, with no confirmation when the green toggle is actually flipped.
findings.norm: Data-sharing settings must name the real recipient, data, purpose and retention, and consequential toggles confirm before applying.
findings.fix: Replace with real provider names and one-line data/retention summaries, and confirm 'Pause all agents?' in a sheet when Model is turned off.

findings.element: 'Not now' button in 'Share recordings with Speech A?' sheet
findings.problem: 'Not now' gives no consequence: will dictation be unavailable, will they be re-asked every tap of the mic? Nor is it clear Allow is permanent or revocable here, though Settings proves it is.
findings.norm: Declining a permission must state the resulting capability loss and where to change it later.
findings.fix: Add 'You can still type. Turn this on anytime in Settings › AI data sharing.' under 'Not now'.

findings.element: Left list rows vs open thread in Inner view
findings.problem: The Inbox agent thread for Ana Ruiz is open on the right, yet no left row ('Ana Ruiz / Re: Pilot timeline') is highlighted as selected; all 'Needs reply' rows carry identical white dots. On the wide Inner display the founder cannot anchor which mail the draft answers.
findings.norm: Master–detail layouts require a persistent selected state in the master list matching the detail pane.
findings.fix: Give the Ana Ruiz row a filled selected background and keep the unread dot distinct from the selection indicator.

findings.element: Composer 'Also ask her for the agenda' with a separate floating '⋮' round button at far right
findings.problem: Inner introduces a second, unlabeled circular overflow button outside the composer that does not exist on the outer thread, competing with the up-arrow and sitting at the far edge—hardest for one-handed reach, and inconsistent with the floating rail used elsewhere.
findings.norm: Keep composer chrome identical across form factors; no unlabeled satellite buttons; primary actions within thumb reach.
findings.fix: Remove the satellite button (fold into the existing Chat menu on the rail) and right-align the send arrow inside the composer as on Duo outer.

findings.element: Chips 'Re: Pilot timeline' and 'Ana Ruiz' directly under the approval card
findings.problem: Two grey pills duplicate information already in the card ('Re: Pilot timeline', 'To Ana Ruiz') with no label or visible action. Founders will tap them expecting navigation and get undefined behaviour.
findings.norm: Every chip must be a labelled, functional filter/link or be removed; no decorative duplicate metadata.
findings.fix: Delete the chips, or turn them into a single labelled link 'Open original email from Ana Ruiz'.

findings.element: Header stack 'Funding room' avatar cluster with 'C' badge and typing indicator in group thread
findings.problem: Two agent shapes (orange Finance triangle, purple Legal droplet) plus an unexplained 'C' overlap the header, and the bottom typing row shows only a purple droplet with '•••' and no name. In the one multi-agent view, attribution—the core value of per-agent shapes—fails at the exact moment of activity, and the always-visible stop square implies a run the bubbles do not explain.
findings.norm: In group agent UIs, every activity indicator is named; avatar clusters explain membership (e.g. 'Finance, Legal + you').
findings.fix: Label typing as 'Legal agent is checking dates…', expand the header to 'Funding room · Finance, Legal' on tap, and remove 'C' or identify it as the user.

findings.element: Menu items 'Clear chat' vs red 'Delete chat'/'Delete group' and 'Open computer' in Chat menus
findings.problem: For a non-technical founder, 'Clear chat' vs 'Delete chat' (and in group, 'Delete group') distinction is nowhere explained in the menu; only group delete gets a confirmation saying messages are removed for everyone. 'Open computer' is jargon with no preview of what opens. Destructive red text-only 'Delete' in confirmations is also weaker than the adjacent bold 'Cancel', inverting prominence.
findings.norm: Destructive actions are verb-labelled with scope ('Delete for everyone'), explained before confirmation, and visually weighted as the deliberate choice in the dialog.
findings.fix: Rename to 'Clear history (keeps the chat)' and 'Delete for everyone…', add subtitles in-menu, and style confirmation Delete as a filled red button.

findings.element: Floating left rail (Back / Page / List / More icons) present in every thread frame
findings.problem: Four icon-only glass buttons with no visible labels; meaning exists only in the separate 'Accessible names' spec column ('Page — Open the page', 'List — Open the to do list' [sic]). A first-time founder must guess, the rail eats ~12% of a 466px-wide screen, pushes chat right, and its top Back sits far from the one-handed thumb zone.
findings.norm: Primary navigation on a narrow phone surface is labelled or uses universally-known glyphs, bottom-anchored for thumb reach; spec annotations are not a substitute for in-UI labels.
findings.fix: Add text labels or a labelled bottom bar for Page/List, fix the 'to do' typo, and keep only Back + More in the rail.

findings.element: Vertical space use in thread frames (e.g. 'Loading', 'Running', 'Offline, message queued')
findings.problem: Roughly the top 55–65% of most frames is empty black; content hugs the composer while the camera pill and '9:41' float in dead space. On a 466x678 outer display the app neither fits more context nor uses the space for status—long drafts will force scrolling the approval card off-screen.
findings.norm: Chat layouts anchor status at top and content continuously; no majority-empty first screen, and approval cards must stay fully visible without scroll.
findings.fix: Pin a compact status/agent header under the title pill, let history fill the space, and cap draft-card height with internal scroll so Edit/Send never leave the screen.

findings.element: Suggestion chips 'Summarize my inbox' / 'Draft a reply to Ana' / 'What is due this week?' under 'Hello! How can I help?'
findings.problem: This is the only genuine first-message state, yet the agent is named 'Chief'—an agent absent from the brief's Inbox/Finance/Legal roster and from every other frame—so a first-time user learns the wrong cast. Chips also wrap unevenly (2+1) with the third orphaned left.
findings.norm: Onboarding surfaces introduce the actual named agents consistently across the product.
findings.fix: Rename to the real default agent (or explain Chief as coordinator of Inbox/Finance/Legal) and lay chips in a single-column list for one-handed tapping.

findings.element: 'Needs approval' pill with chevron beneath the user bubble in 'Approval pending' (4th frame)
findings.problem: The same product expresses approval three ways: gold pill on the card, gold pill in headers, and here a dark collapsible pill with a yellow dot under the user's own message, separated from the draft it controls. Tapping target and destination are ambiguous.
findings.norm: One status component, one placement (on the object it describes), reused identically everywhere.
findings.fix: Standardise on the on-card 'Needs approval' pill from PG-A-Thread and make it scroll to/highlight the draft card.

findings.element: Skeleton bubbles in 'Loading' frame and 'Could not refresh / Try again' banner
findings.problem: Loading shows three anonymous grey blobs with an enabled composer and no 'Loading…' label—indistinguishable from a broken empty chat. 'Could not refresh' gives no time reference ('showing mail from 9:12'), so the founder may act on stale inbox data between meetings.
findings.norm: Loading and stale states are verbally labelled, input is either disabled or declared safe, and stale content carries its age.
findings.fix: Add 'Loading messages…' with the skeletons, disable composer send until loaded, and change the refresh banner to 'Couldn't refresh—showing 9:12 AM inbox · Try again'.

findings.element: 'Add a recipient' in 'Empty recipient' frame
findings.problem: The safeguard works—Send greys out—but the gold 'Add a recipient' text gives no hint it is tappable (no chevron/field styling) and the card otherwise looks complete, so a hurried founder reads the state as cosmetic rather than blocking.
findings.norm: Missing required fields use field affordance and a one-line blocking explanation next to the disabled action.
findings.fix: Render 'To' as an empty tappable field 'Add a recipient…' and add 'Add a recipient to send' as helper text above the disabled Send.

findings.element: Colour system across all screens: green iOS toggles, gold 'Needs approval', red errors, blue/green/orange/purple agent marks on near-black
findings.problem: The brief promises monochrome with colour reserved for per-agent identity, but system-green toggles in Settings are the loudest colour in the product and read as ' Praci brand/active' rather than agent identity; gold approval and red error then compete as a third and fourth semantic palette with no legend.
findings.norm: Reserve saturated colour for defined semantics; platform toggles should adopt the app accent or be explicitly excepted in the system.
findings.fix: Tint Settings switches to the neutral/monochrome accent (or document green=on as a system exception) and publish one legend: agent colour = identity, gold = your approval, red = error.

findings.element: 'Archive this chat?' confirmation over still-visible 'Edit/Send' card
findings.problem: The dialog correctly says 'It moves to Archived. You can restore it.', but the live approval card behind it still shows a white 'Send', inviting the interpretation that archiving and sending are related, and nothing says the pending draft survives archiving.
findings.norm: Confirmation dialogs state the fate of in-progress work (unsent draft) explicitly.
findings.fix: Change body to 'It moves to Archived. Your unsent draft to Ana Ruiz is kept and restored with the chat.'

excellent: PG-A-Thread.png — 'Re: Pilot timeline' approval card: recipient, full draft text, gold 'Needs approval' pill, secondary 'Edit' and one prominent white 'Send' is exactly the explicit-approval pattern promised; 'Archive confirmation' likewise states reversibility ('You can restore it.').

ts_row0.png — 'Failed' frame: red-outlined bubble plus 'Not sent · Retry' in one line gives cause and recovery without a modal; 'Refused: file too large' names the 25 MB limit and a 'Remove file' action.
ts_row1.png — 'New messages, scrolled up': 'NEW' divider plus a floating 'Jump to latest' pill is textbook chat behaviour and ideal one-handed.

ts_row4.png — 'Running' frames: agent avatar with progress arc and '•••' bubble, and the mic morphing into a stop control, make agent activity legible at a glance; 'Approval pending, typing' keeps Edit/Send visible while composing.

PG-A-GroupThread.png — Finance agent (orange triangle) vs Legal agent (purple droplet) with name labels above each bubble delivers the promised per-agent shape/colour identity; 'Delete Funding room?' states scope and irreversibility ('removed for everyone. This cannot be undone.').

PG-B-Consent.png — Consent sheet hierarchy: plain-language data sentence, one prominent 'Allow', quieter 'Not now', and a 'Privacy details' link is the right shape for informed consent (content gaps notwithstanding); Settings shows the dependency 'Turning off Model A pauses all agents.'

Inner.png — Dual-pane Inbox + Inbox agent thread fits one 890x626 screen with correct counts ('Needs reply 3', 'Other mail today 24') and the same approval card, proving the wide layout without inventing new patterns.

result.verdict: Praci demonstrates strong craft in its dark monochrome visual language, inline approval architecture, and unusually thorough edge-case state coverage, but contains critical safety and interaction flaws—most notably enabling the primary 'Send' CTA while an agent is mid-stream editing a draft, keeping an active 'Send' button when an oversize attachment blocks submission, and exposing a 'Stop' button where users expect 'Send' while typing during an active agent run.

findings.element: Mail approval card ('Send' button in 'Agent editing the draft' frame)
findings.problem: While the agent is actively modifying the email draft (indicated by the 'Updating' badge and streaming text cursor in the body), the 'Edit' button is disabled, but the primary 'Send' button remains fully enabled and styled as the prominent solid-white CTA.
findings.norm: Destructive or external-facing commit actions (like sending an email to a customer) must never be enabled while the underlying content is actively mutating or streaming, as the user cannot verify what will actually be sent.
findings.fix: Disable the 'Send' button (matching the disabled styling used in the 'Empty recipient' frame) whenever the draft card is in the 'Updating' state, and re-enable it only after the agent finishes streaming changes.

findings.element: Composer Send button ('Composer with an oversize file' frame)
findings.problem: The composer displays an error chip ('! pilot-deck.pdf') and explicit blocking helper text ('pilot-deck.pdf is over 25 MB. Remove it to send.'), yet the circular Send button (up-arrow) at the bottom-right of the composer is rendered in its fully active, solid-white primary state.
findings.norm: When form or composer validation blocks submission, the submit button must visually and functionally reflect the disabled state so users do not repeatedly tap an active-looking CTA that cannot succeed.
findings.fix: Render the composer Send button in a disabled, low-contrast state whenever an attachment exceeds the file size limit, and include the file size ('48 MB') inside the red attachment pill so the user immediately sees why it failed validation.

findings.element: Composer right action button ('Running, text typed' frame)
findings.problem: When the user types a follow-up message ('Also check Ana') while the agent is running, the button inside the right edge of the text input remains the solid-white 'Stop' button (square icon) rather than a Send/Queue control. A one-handed user who finishes typing and reflexively taps the bottom-right composer button will accidentally abort the agent's current run instead of submitting their text.
findings.norm: Input submission controls and process cancellation controls must not occupy the same spatial slot while text is entered; typing into a composer creates a strong expectation that the trailing button inside the text field submits the typed text.
findings.fix: Move the 'Stop' action out of the text input's trailing submit slot when the user is typing (for example, place a 'Stop' pill alongside the agent's typing indicator bubble above the composer), or allow the trailing button to queue/send the typed message without killing the active run.

findings.element: Mail approval card 'Send' button vs. Composer Send icon ('Approval pending, typing' frame and 'Inner.png')
findings.problem: When a user types a modification request in the composer ('Add Jordan on Cc' in ts_row4.png or 'Also ask her for the agenda' in Inner.png) below an unapproved draft card, the composer's Send button is demoted to a bare, borderless arrow icon while the draft card's 'Send' button directly above it remains bright solid white. A rushed user typing in the composer can easily tap the prominent white 'Send' button right above the input field, sending the unedited email before the agent adds Jordan on Cc.
findings.norm: Visual hierarchy must follow the user's active focus; when the composer has active text focus and typed content, the composer's submit action must have clear button affordance, and competing commit buttons directly above the keyboard/composer should not overshadow it.
findings.fix: Give the composer's Send button a distinct circular button container when text is entered, and visually de-emphasize the draft card's 'Send' button from solid white to secondary fill while the user is actively typing a follow-up instruction in the composer.

findings.element: Consent sheet and Settings toggles ('Speech, first use' and 'Settings, AI data sharing')
findings.problem: First, the brief specifies that the left panel of PG-B-Consent should be the first-visit sheet asking to share data with the AI model provider before using agents, but the mockup instead shows a 'Speech, first use' microphone consent sheet. Second, both panels expose cryptic placeholder names ('Model A', 'Speech A', 'Memory A') that mean nothing to a non-technical founder. Third, the green iOS toggle switches violate the app's strict monochrome design language.
findings.norm: Privacy and data-sharing consent screens must clearly name the actual service or plain-language capability for non-technical users, cover the primary blocker flow (model provider consent), and adhere to the product's monochrome color system.
findings.fix: Add the primary first-visit AI Model Provider consent sheet, replace placeholder names ('Model A', 'Speech A', 'Memory A') with real provider names or clear functional labels (e.g., 'Language model', 'Voice transcription', 'Conversation memory'), and style active toggles in high-contrast monochrome white/grey rather than system green.

findings.element: Offline status banner ('Offline, nothing queued' vs. 'Offline, message queued')
findings.problem: In 'Offline, nothing queued', a top banner clearly explains: 'Offline. Messages send when you reconnect.' However, in 'Offline, message queued', as soon as the user sends a message that gets stuck in 'Waiting to send', the top offline banner disappears completely, removing the explanation for why the message is not sending.
findings.norm: System status banners explaining connectivity loss must persist while messages are queued offline so the user understands the root cause of the 'Waiting to send' state.
findings.fix: Keep the 'Offline. Messages send when you reconnect.' banner visible at the top of the thread whenever the device is offline, especially when one or more messages are in the 'Waiting to send' state.

findings.element: Oversize file error bubble ('Refused: file too large' frame)
findings.problem: First, showing a 48 MB file already sent as a chat bubble contradicts 'ts_row1.png' ('Composer with an oversize file'), where the exact same 48 MB file is blocked in the composer before sending. Second, the recovery action 'x Remove file' on a sent message that says 'Attached the pilot deck.' is ambiguous: it is unclear whether tapping 'Remove file' will immediately send the text 'Attached the pilot deck.' without the attachment, delete the entire bubble, or return the message to the composer.
findings.norm: Validation should prevent impossible states consistently, and error recovery actions on multi-part messages (text + attachment) must make clear whether the accompanying text will be sent, edited, or discarded.
findings.fix: If a file fails post-send validation, provide an 'Edit in composer' or 'Delete message' action rather than 'Remove file', so the user never accidentally sends a message saying 'Attached the pilot deck.' with the attachment stripped out.

findings.element: First-message prompt suggestions ('Chief' thread, first column)
findings.problem: The three starter prompt pills ('Summarize my inbox', 'Draft a reply to Ana', 'What is due this week?') use the exact same dark surface fill, corner radius, typography, and left-aligned placement as the agent's incoming greeting bubble ('Hello! How can I help?') directly above them.
findings.norm: Interactive prompt suggestions (which represent actions the user can send) must be visually distinct from incoming agent messages so first-time users immediately recognize them as tappable user prompts.
findings.fix: Differentiate prompt suggestion chips from incoming agent bubbles by right-aligning them above the composer, adding a subtle border stroke or trailing upward-arrow/sparkle icon, and increasing vertical separation from the agent's greeting bubble.

findings.element: Disconnected model state ('Not sent: No model connected' frame)
findings.problem: When no AI model is connected (or AI data sharing is paused), the composer remains active and invites the user to type and send 'Hello', only to fail after submission with technical jargon ('Not sent: No model connected + Connect').
findings.norm: Prevent errors before input: if a required global dependency (like model provider consent or connection) is missing, disable or replace the composer with an inline setup prompt rather than letting the user type and fail.
findings.fix: When no model is connected or AI data sharing is turned off in Settings, replace or overlay the composer with a clear banner ('AI agents are paused. Connect a model to start chatting.' with a 'Connect' button) before the user types a message.

findings.element: Team computer card ('Inbox agent opened Team computer' frame)
findings.problem: First, the 'Take control' button is styled as the prominent solid-white primary CTA—identical to 'Send' on an email approval card—encouraging a non-technical phone user to interrupt the agent and open a remote desktop view unnecessarily. Second, the dark preview rectangle inside the card is empty and misaligned, stopping roughly 35px short of the card's right padding edge.
findings.norm: Reserve the single high-contrast primary button per view for actions the user is required to take (such as approving a blocked action); optional override actions like taking over an agent's virtual desktop should use secondary button styling.
findings.fix: Style 'Take control' as a secondary pill button (matching 'Edit' on the draft card) unless the agent is explicitly blocked waiting for human input, and fix the width of the inner screen preview container so its right margin matches its left margin (12–16px).

findings.element: Archive confirmation modal ('Archive confirmation' frame)
findings.problem: Tapping 'Archive' in the chat menu triggers a blocking confirmation alert ('Archive this chat? It moves to Archived. You can restore it. Cancel / Archive'), even though archiving is completely non-destructive and the resulting 'Archived' view immediately displays a prominent 'Restore' button at the top.
findings.norm: Blocking confirmation dialogs should be reserved for irreversible destructive actions (like 'Delete chat' or 'Delete group'); reversible organization actions like 'Archive' should execute immediately with an easy undo/restore affordance.
findings.fix: Remove the modal confirmation step for 'Archive' and transition directly to the archived state with the top 'Restore' banner (or show a brief undo toast).

findings.element: Mail approval card ('Add a recipient' in 'Empty recipient' frame)
findings.problem: In the 'Empty recipient' frame, the missing recipient placeholder ('Add a recipient') uses the exact same amber/yellow text color as the non-interactive 'Needs approval' status badge directly above it, with no button container, plus icon, or input affordance to indicate whether 'Add a recipient' is directly tappable or requires tapping 'Edit'.
findings.norm: Interactive placeholders and non-interactive status badges should not share the exact same visual treatment without clear tap affordances.
findings.fix: Give '+ Add a recipient' a subtle pill border or leading '+' icon so it clearly reads as a tappable target, or automatically focus the recipient field in edit mode when a draft has no recipient.

findings.element: Left floating navigation rail vs. content column (all Duo outer frames)
findings.problem: Placing the 4-icon floating glass rail vertically down the left edge below the camera cutout and '9:41' clock forces the entire chat thread and settings content to indent by ~46–60px across the full height of the 466px screen, wasting ~12% of horizontal width in the lower two-thirds of the viewport while leaving only a ~2px gap between the floating rail and message elements.
findings.norm: On compact mobile viewports, persistent navigation chrome should minimize horizontal encroachment on the primary reading and composing column and maintain at least 8–12px of clearance from content.
findings.fix: Consolidate top navigation into a single horizontal header bar alongside the agent pill (moving 'Page', 'List', and 'Chat menu' to the top-right header area), freeing the full width of the screen for messages, approval cards, and the composer.

findings.element: Right-pane navigation rail and bottom-right 'Chat menu' button
findings.problem: On the inner display, the floating rail moves to the top-right with only two icons ('Page' and 'List'), while the three-dots 'Chat menu' button is split off to the bottom-right corner directly beside the composer's Send arrow. Meanwhile, the chat messages and draft card still leave a wide empty column down the right side below the short floating rail.
findings.norm: Keep related thread-level navigation controls grouped together consistently across device postures, and avoid placing a menu containing destructive actions ('Clear chat', 'Delete chat') right next to the primary composer Send button.
findings.fix: Keep the three-dots 'Chat menu' icon inside the top-right floating control group with 'Page' and 'List', and allow the composer and message column to align cleanly without a competing button at the bottom-right.

findings.element: Context pills below approval card ('Re: Pilot timeline' and 'Ana Ruiz')
findings.problem: Two dark pills ('Re: Pilot timeline' and 'Ana Ruiz') float between the mail approval card and the composer with no leading icons, no dismiss 'x' buttons, and no visual tether to either the card above or the composer below, leaving their purpose and interactivity ambiguous.
findings.norm: Context chips or quick-action pills must clearly communicate whether they are attached context for the composer (inside the composer border with a remove affordance) or source citations attached to the agent's response (with mail/contact icons).
findings.fix: If these pills represent context attached to the user's follow-up prompt, move them inside the composer container above the text input (consistent with attachment chips in ts_row1.png); if they are source citations for the agent's draft, add leading mail/contact icons and attach them to the agent turn.

findings.element: Scrolled-up state mockups ('New messages, scrolled up' in ts_row1.png and Col 4 in ts_row3.png)
findings.problem: In both frames demonstrating scrolled-up floating pills ('Jump to latest v' in ts_row1.png and 'Needs approval v' in ts_row3.png), the screen contains only 2 short bubbles positioned near the bottom with 350–400px of empty black space above them, and in ts_row1.png the 'NEW' message ('Ana confirmed 10am.') is already completely visible on screen above 'Jump to latest'.
findings.norm: Scroll-to-bottom / jump-to-anchor indicators should only appear when the target content is actually clipped below the viewport fold in a populated thread.
findings.fix: Populate scrolled-up state mockups with enough prior conversation history to fill the viewport height so the off-screen target below the fold is logically implied.

findings.element: Inbox list timestamps and unread hierarchy ('Inner.png' left pane)
findings.problem: First, under 'Needs reply 3', the top email is timestamped '10:30 AM' (and device time is '9:41'), yet 'Other mail today 24' lists emails from '3:25 PM', '3:02 PM', and '2:41 PM' on the same day. Second, read emails without a white dot ('Example Weekly', 'Deals Daily') use the exact same bright white text contrast as unread emails with a white dot.
findings.norm: Mockup timestamps should be chronologically coherent, and read items in an inbox list should use muted secondary text contrast so unread/actionable items stand out at a glance.
findings.fix: Adjust 'Other mail today' timestamps to earlier morning times (e.g., '9:15 AM', '8:50 AM', '7:30 AM') and dim the sender/subject text weight and opacity on read rows that lack an unread indicator dot.

findings.element: Accessible names table ('Round square' label in PG-A-Thread.png vs. PG-A-GroupThread.png) and cropped frame titles (ts_row1.png, ts_row3.png, ts_row4.png)
findings.problem: The accessible name for the exact same stop button ('Round square') is documented as 'Stop' in PG-A-Thread.png but as 'Stop the run' in PG-A-GroupThread.png. Additionally, the row exports in ts_row1.png, ts_row3.png, and ts_row4.png clip the frame titles along the top and bottom edges.
findings.norm: Accessibility labels for identical controls must be consistent across single and group threads, and specification boards should be exported without slicing frame titles.
findings.fix: Standardize the accessible label for the stop control across all thread types (e.g., 'Stop agent') and adjust artboard slice bounds on the ThreadStates rows so all frame headers remain legible.

excellent: Comprehensive state coverage across 20+ conversation edge cases—including offline queuing, oversize attachments, mid-stream draft updates, replaced drafts, archived restore, and computer-use blocks—gives engineering a nearly complete behavioral specification.
The inline mail approval card ('Re: Pilot timeline') is clean, scannable, and keeps the founder in the conversation flow without forcing a full-screen modal compose view for routine replies.

Distinct per-agent geometric avatars and colors (blue rounded-rect for Inbox agent, orange triangle for Finance agent, purple droplet for Legal agent) create instant sender recognition inside a restrained dark monochrome interface.
Including explicit 'Accessible names' specification tables alongside the UI frames demonstrates strong commitment to VoiceOver usability from the earliest design phase.

Inline error states on failed messages ('Not sent / Retry', 'No model connected / + Connect') pair clear red outline affordances with immediate, single-tap recovery actions right below the affected bubble.
